title: Action de Galois sur Teichmüller : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting: Σ = P^1(C) with its real equator Σ_R and three marked real points R_0, R_1, R_∞. The previous page takes the standard barycentric subdivision of the resulting map (the 'carte' of the equator plus three points). This gives 12 flag triangles D_r = P_ε Q_i R_{ωi}. Here r = (i, ω, ε): i is one of the three marked points, ω one of two directions along the equator, and ε one of the two hemispheres with poles P_±. Σ̃ is the sphere with small discs removed around the three points, homotopy equivalent to Σ* = P^1 − {0,1,∞}. On Σ̃ each flag triangle becomes a quadrilateral. The enlarged region Σ̃_r = D̃_r ∪ τ(D̃_r) ∪ σ̃_i(D̃_r) ∪ σ̃_{ωi}(D̃_r) is the triangle together with its reflections across its three sides. Here τ is complex conjugation and the σ̃ are the involutions of S_3.

This page does four things:
(1) It draws the standard region Σ̃_r on the sphere, bounded by the contour P_+Q_1R_0^-S_0^+R_0^+S_0^-P_-Q_∞R_1^-S_1^+P_+.
(2) It notes that Γ = S_3 × {1, τ}, of order 12 (the automorphisms of (P^1, {0,1,∞}, real structure)), permutes the 12 regions simply transitively.
(3) Each Σ̃_r is simply connected. So the fundamental group based at the region, π_r = π_1(Σ̃; Σ̃_r) ≅ π_1(Σ*; Σ*_r), is defined up to unique isomorphism. This is the 'fundamental group at a 1-connected base region', which is equivalent to a tangential or extended base point.
(4) These 12 groups are linked by the canonical transitive system of transition isomorphisms. One also has 'isomorphismes d'épinglage' Ψ_r : π_{0,3} → π_r, with π_{0,3} the standard free group on two generators. Ψ_r is obtained by composing Ψ_ε^{ω,i} : π_{0,3} → π_1(Σ̃, P_ε) with φ_r^{-1}. Here φ_r : π_r → π_1(Σ̃, P_ε) is the transition isomorphism attached to the 1-connected region Σ_r and the point P_ε ∈ Σ_r.

Purpose: to build a Γ-equivariant, combinatorially rigid system of base points and pinnings of π_1 of P^1 − 3 points. This is the basic building block for gluing ('Lego') the Teichmüller tower and for writing the Galois action, including the S_3 and complex-conjugation symmetries. The next page specializes to base points at the R_i^ω and to orientation choices.
errors: The equation number (42) appears twice; the first was probably meant as (41 bis) or something similar.

No mathematical error. Simple transitivity of a group of order 12 on 12 flag regions and the simple connectivity of the star-shaped union are both correct. Ψ_r's dependence on the chosen paths is absorbed by the 1-connectedness, as claimed.

ideas.what: Fundamental group based at a simply connected region (rather than a point), giving canonically isomorphic groups via transitive systems of transition isomorphisms
ideas.modern_name: fundamental groupoid with base 'points' = contractible subsets; tangential/extended base points
ideas.usually_credited_to: Deligne (1989, Le groupe fondamental de la droite projective moins trois points); Ihara; Nakamura
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (1984), base points for the Teichmüller tower; SGA1 transitive systems of isomorphisms

ideas.what: Simply transitive action of Γ = S_3 × Z/2 (with complex conjugation) on the 12 flag regions of the barycentric subdivision of the real-equator map of P^1 − {0,1,∞}
ideas.modern_name: flags of the dessin/real structure of P^1 minus 3 points; automorphism group of the triangulated sphere
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme discusses barycentric subdivisions and the role of complex conjugation, but not this exact setup

ideas.what: Pinning isomorphisms Ψ_r : π_{0,3} → π_r, compatible with Γ, defined by composing a standard pinning with a transition isomorphism
ideas.modern_name: choices of standard generators at tangential base points; S_3-equivariant system used in GT (Drinfeld, Ihara)

missed.claim: A systematic Γ = S_3 × ⟨τ⟩-equivariant atlas of 12 base regions on P^1 − 3 points with explicit pinnings, including complex conjugation. This is a careful combinatorial precursor of the base-point bookkeeping later done for GT. Content-wise it is standard today, but it documents Grothendieck's explicit handling of the real structure in the Lego construction.
missed.quote: Les régions Σ̃_r sont permutées de façon simplement transitive par Γ = S_3×(1,τ). Elles sont simplement connexes
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Mainly historical. It shows that Grothendieck's tangential-base-point formalism around 1978–81 already incorporated the full 12-element symmetry group, including τ. This is relevant to the extended GT incorporating complex conjugation, but it is not a new result.

deep.surprise_reason: This is a careful but routine setup of base regions and pinnings for π_1(P^1 − 3 points) with S_3 × Z/2 symmetry. The ideas are now standard (tangential base points, GT bookkeeping); the interest is historical priority and detail only.
transcription_corrections: π_r = π_i^{ω,ε} (not π_i^{ω,i}) in both occurrences; likewise Ψ_r = Ψ_ε^{ω,i}.
The label in the first formula is a crossed-out or renumbered '(41 bis)'-type label, not a clean (42).

'des sont gro... pour identifier' is hard to read; probably something like 'ils sont garantis / on s'en sert pour identifier tous ces groupes entre eux'. The 'à l'aide des op. de Γ' reading is plausible.
'(Ψ_r composants' is a crossed or abandoned fragment ('Ψ_r composé...'), replaced by 'en composant'.
In the figure the marked point on the left equator is Q_1, alongside Q_∞; there is a curved arrow labeled G (or C) inside the hatched region, possibly an orientation mark.
